hens_rule_text: No numeric cap on hens was found in the Lexington-Fayette Urban County code sections located; chickens must be confined to the owner's property and not run at large.
permit_notes: No permit requirement was found in the code provisions located (Chapter 4, Animals and Fowl); some secondary sources mention a permit but this was not confirmed in the code text itself.
setback_notes: No specific setback distance from neighboring dwellings was found in the sections reviewed (Sec. 4-8, Sec. 4-10).
coop_rules: Fowl must be confined to the owner's property at all times; running at large is prohibited (Sec. 4-10, Fowl going at large).
zoning_notes: As of 1 November 2025, an Urban County Council ordinance limits households outside agricultural zones to no more than 1 rooster; this was passed in response to noise complaints and raised the maximum fine for animal-code violations to $100 per day.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Lexington-Fayette Urban County Code Chapter 4 (Animals and Fowl), Sec. 4-8 and Sec. 4-10; rooster limit added by a 2025 amending ordinance effective November 1, 2025

sources.name: Lexington-Fayette Urban County Code, Sec. 4-10, Fowl going at large
Spectrum News 1, Lexington residents could see limits on rooster ownership (Aug 2025)

research_notes: amlegal.com is Cloudflare-blocked from this machine, so the base rules come from WebSearch's extracts of the code's fowl sections, which did not surface a hen cap, permit rule or setback distance; those fields are left unknown rather than guessed. A 2025 news article (confirmed by search, not the ordinance text itself) describes a new one-rooster-per-household limit outside agricultural zones effective November 1, 2025, so roosters are marked conditional. An unrelated Lexington, Virginia news article about a different small town's 2019 hen ordinance was found during research and explicitly excluded as it does not describe this city.
